correctness.rationale: Theorem 4.1 of arXiv:2611.14300v1 divides the numerator and denominator of reduced representatives separately. With join primes from Theorem 3.14 this is exactly the displayed sign-and-magnitude order. The component argument using minimal nonfaces independently proves the needed join factorization, including isolated vertices. The sign retraction s respects the order, is equivariant, and satisfies s≤id, so the order homotopy given by this natural transformation fixes the retracted subposet. That subposet is the nonempty proper face poset of the cross-polytope, giving its barycentric subdivision. Orthogonal signed permutations act on its reduced integral top homology by determinant, including the swap of the two points in rank one. For rigidity, opposition of signed atoms is recognized by the failure of a common upper bound. After canceling a signed permutation, an automorphism fixes each atom. Elements with just that atom below them form a chain of type 1<2<… and are fixed pointwise; for a general element each coordinate is recovered from the largest axis point below it. This also independently verifies the predecessor induction. The equivariant equivalence descends to the inversion quotient, and radial projection gives the antipodal sphere quotient RP^(r−1), including rank one; it gives H₁(RP²;Z)=Z/2. In the full puncture the same retraction works, with countably infinitely many primes (all discrete simplicial complexes on ≥2 vertices are join indecomposable, as is the one-vertex complex). Compact sphere images in the CW realization lie in finite subcomplexes; putting their finite signed support in the cone of an unused signed vertex contracts the maps, and also connects any two points. Whitehead then yields contractibility. McCord gives the weak comparison to the Alexandrov space; no ordinary equivalence with the Hausdorff sphere is needed. The checker was inspected but not executed; no finite computed invariant is required by the finding.
